answer: A useful mechanism is a nontransferable, time-locked stake attached to each agent’s identity: agents earn access to valuable tasks only after behaving consistently across repeated interactions, while fraud reports backed by evidence can slash the stake. The stake acts as an anchor, and a reputation reef forms as independent counterparties corroborate history. A velvet-smooth flood of fresh identities still cannot inherit that record; the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it, so scaling a sybil campaign becomes costly.
